STEP 1 - Scene: A chicken salad: mixed greens (spinach/baby leaves) topped with diced grilled chicken and crumbled feta-style cheese. Served in a large bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white bowl, roughly 22 cm diameter (between side plate and dinner plate). Area = 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm². Food fills nearly the whole bowl, so coverage is about 95%.

STEP 3 - Items: mixed leafy greens (spinach, baby lettuce), diced cooked chicken breast, crumbled white cheese (feta-style). No visible dressing pooling.

STEP 4 - Area (percent of vessel area):
- Mixed leafy greens: 45% (171 cm²)
- Diced chicken: 30% (114 cm²)
- Crumbled cheese: 20% (76 cm²)
Total ≈ 95%, consistent with near-full coverage.

STEP 5 - Volume (area x typical height, outer envelope):
- Greens: 171 cm² x 3 cm ≈ 513 ml
- Chicken: 114 cm² x 2 cm ≈ 228 ml
- Cheese: 76 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 114 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Greens: 513 ml x 0.15 ≈ 77 g
- Chicken: 228 ml x 1.0 ≈ 228 g
- Cheese: 114 ml x 0.9 ≈ 103 g

Hmm, chicken at full density over-weights the pile given visible gaps between cubes; I keep the stated density as the only reduction per the method. Total ≈ 408 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Greens: 77 g x 20 kcal/100 g ≈ 15 kcal
- Chicken: 228 g x 165 kcal/100 g ≈ 376 kcal
- Cheese: 103 g x 265 kcal/100 g ≈ 273 kcal
Total ≈ 664 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A bowl nearly full of greens, chicken and cheese at about 400 g and roughly 650 kcal is plausible for a large chicken salad. Cheese at 265 kcal/100 g is typical for feta-style cheese; the estimate could be somewhat high if the cheese and chicken are sparser than the envelope suggests.
